tells.1: Uses formulaic marketing language like 'practical way to get a fuller picture' and a symmetrical, polished structure.
tells.2: Ends abruptly after the price with no conversational close; relies on the standard 'baseline to track over time' phrase.
tells.3: AI-style benefit wrap-up: 'practical way to get a fuller picture... and more out of the checkup.'
tells.5: Formal, padded phrasing ('it is highly beneficial to have annual blood work done') and redundant list of markers.
tells.6: Flat, generic summary with no hook or personality; bluntly ends with 'costs $129.'

reason: Version 4 sounds the most like a skilled, natural clinic writer because it uses concrete conversational phrasing ('shots,' 'hits 7,' 'something's off') while still covering the medical content and a clear CTA. It avoids the formulaic marketing phrases and stiffness present in other versions.
